text:
A Bandidos gang member says he couldn’t remember a lucrative invoice because it brought up bad memories of having been told there was a contract out on his life.
Former CFMEU member and bikie, Joel Leavitt faced a second day of examination by the royal commission into alleged corruption across Victoria’s construction sector on Wednesday.
Questioning returned to a $165,000 invoice paid to Leavitt’s now defunct company, JVL Consulting, by union-aligned subcontractor BK Labour Hire in July 2025.
When shown a copy of the invoice Leavitt was unable to recall anything to do with it, or even give a clear answer as to what services his former company provided.
Counsel assisting the commission, Chris Carr SC asked why Leavitt appeared to become uncomfortable when asked about the invoice.
Leavitt blamed his poor memory on having ADHD, as well as PTSD from being shot in May 2023.
“Around that time I actually got told by gang squad that there was a contract on my life,” he said.
“So it brought back some uncomfortable memories.
“That’s why I blocked out a lot of that time.”
Commissioner Chris Kourakis AC warned Leavitt it was an offence to fail to answer questions put to him by the commission, something he said could ultimately be tested in a courtroom.
“I’ve been shot … I’ve had drug issues … I am answering these to the best of my recollection,” Leavitt replied.
“How do you think you would act if you’d ever been shot?”
After the commission briefly adjourned for Leavitt to speak with his lawyers, the bikie returned to the stand saying JVL Consulting provided safety advice to companies.
“Maybe helping them out with their procedures and policies and stuff like that,” he said.
The commission viewed a copy of Leavitt’s bank statement at the time which fluctuated between $0, down to minus $20, before the $165,000 landed in his account.
“Everyone likes money. I’m sure all youse are on good money for this,” said Leavitt, addressing the bar table.
Kourakis informed Leavitt the commission had evidence he did not do any work for BK Labour.
He said an inference that could be made is Leavitt was “standing over” BK Labour for the payment because he needed money.
“If that’s the way you want to look at it commissioner,” Leavitt replied.
Carr asked if Leavitt knew something about BK Labour that the company would have wanted to keep quiet.
“Is the conclusion the commission should draw is that you just stood over them with some sort of explicit or implied threat of violence?” Carr asked.
“I’d like to talk to my counsel before I answer that,” Leavitt replied.
The inquiry continues.
digest_he:
ג'ואי לביט, חבר כנופיית האופנוענים בנדידוס וחבר איגוד לשעבר, הופיע ליום הדיונים השני בפני ועדה מלכותית החוקרת שחיתות לכאורה בענף הבנייה במדינת ויקטוריה שבאוסטרליה. החקירה התמקדה בחשבונית על סך 165 אלף דולר ששולמה לחברה שבבעלותו לשעבר על ידי קבלן משנה המזוהה עם איגוד עובדים.

בעדותו טען לביט כי אינו מסוגל להיזכר באילו שירותים סיפקה חברתו, וייחס את זיכרונו הלוקה להפרעת קשב וריכוז ולפוסט-טראומה בעקבות ירי לעברו. הנציב העומד בראש הוועדה הציע כי החברה שילמה את הסכום תחת לחץ או איומים מצידו עקב מצבו הכלכלי הקשה, אך לביט בחר להתייעץ עם עורכי דינו טרם מתן תשובה סופית בנושא.
